Author: Juvvadi Sridevi
Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Juvvadi Sridevi
 Criminal Petition No.14815 of 2024
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') by petitioner- accused No.1 seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.2356 of 2023 pending on the file of the learned XIV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, registered for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

entities.text: XIV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Mr. K.S.Suneel, learned counsel for the petitioner.
The respondent No.2-de facto complainant has expired and there is no representation on his behalf.
Hence, Mr. M.Ramachandra Reddy, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1- State, is heard on behalf of respondent No.2-de facto complainant also.
Perused the material on record.
3. The case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the petitioner- accused No.1 is the Chairman and Managing Director of M/s. Country Club Hospitality and Holidays Limited.

entities.text: Country Club Hospitality and Holidays Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is alleged that on the instructions of petitioner-accused No.1, accused Nos.2 and 3, on 03.02.2016, induced the de facto complainant to part with a sum of Rs.1,65,000/- towards the purchase of a product in which he was not interested, and further obtained his signature on an agreement without allowing him to read the terms and conditions therein.
Subsequently, upon returning home, the de facto complainant noticed several discrepancies in the documents.

On 05.02.2016, when he, along with his wife, approached the accused to seek clarification of the terms and requested for cancellation of their membership,
the accused informed them that the amount paid was non-refundable.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the complaint does not disclose the name of petitioner-accused No.1 nor any specific overt act was attributed to him.
Despite his name not being mentioned in the complaint, he was arrayed as accused No.1 in the charge sheet.
The petitioner-accused No.1 had no knowledge of the transaction between the Company and the de facto complainant.

The petitioner and the de facto complainant have amicably settled their disputes between them and entered into a deed of compromise, dated 15.02.2016, under which the petitioner paid Rs.1,40,000/- to the de facto complainant by way of a Demand Draft bearing No.967254, dated 15.09.2019, and in turn, the de facto complainant agreed to withdraw the present complaint.

Hence,
he prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioner-accused No.1.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor submits that the de facto complainant approached the Country Club, of which petitioner-accused No.1 is the Managing Director.
During the course of investigation, as his involvement was elicited, charge sheet was filed against him.
There are specific allegations against the petitioner and the truth or otherwise of the allegations levelled against him can only be known after conducting full-fledged trial before the trial Court.

Hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition.
6.

A perusal of the record discloses that the alleged incident occurred on 03.02.2016, whereas the present complaint was lodged on 12.02.2016, i.e., there is a delay of more than 9 days in lodging the complaint.
The reason for such delay remained unexplained.

In the charge sheet or in the statement of de facto complainant recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., no specific overt act is attributed with regard to the complicity of petitioner-accused No.1 nor was it averred that he had knowledge of the transaction, except stating that he is the Managing Director of Country Club.
Section 420 of IPC attracts only when there is inducement to defraud with dishonest intention from the inception and there should be mens rea at the time of inducement.

In the present case, no such ingredients are forthcoming from the entire record against the petitioner-accused No.1.
7.
Furthermore, the petitioner-accused No.1 and de facto complainant have amicably settled their disputes and entered into a deed of compromise, dated 15.02.2016.

As per the said compromise, the petitioner-accused No.1 paid Rs.1,40,000/- to the de facto complainant by way of a Demand Draft bearing No.967254, dated 15.09.2019 and in turn, the de facto complainant agreed to withdraw the present complaint.
It is further brought to the notice of this Court that the de facto complainant has expired.

In the compromise deed itself, the de facto complainant himself has unequivocally stated that he has no claims against petitioner-accused No.1.
8.

In view of the above, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings against the petitioner-accused No.1 in C.C.No.2356 of 2023 pending on the file of the learned XIV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, are hereby quashed
